description.narrative:
A new agreement was signed in May 2023 between the Ministry of Labour and the General Federation of Trade Unions (GFJTU) regarding the issuance of flexible work permits for Syrian refugee labour for the period May 2023-May 2025. This new agreement opens up the issuance of work permits for Syrian refugees to 123 occupational groups, while the previous agreement (covering the period 2017-2022) was for only two sectors (agriculture and construction).
In 2022-23, the General Federation of Jordanian Trade Unions, issued more than 37,000 flexible work permits for Syrian refugees which allow them to access formal employment (meaning access to jobs with social protection). This measure improved compliance with labour law and, as a result, improved workers protection. With the support of the United States, the European Union, and the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the ILO supported the institutional capacity of the General Federation of Jordanian Trade Unions (GFJTU), the sole authorized body by the Ministry of Labour (MoL) to issue Work Permits (WP) to Syrian refugees in Jordan.
The support provided by the ILO enhanced GFJTU's ability to deliver effectively on the ground. More specifically the support provided facilitated the issurance of work permits efficiently and in particular availed the capacity GFJTU to issue the permits for non-Jordanian workers.

Output 3.5. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement labour market programmes and employment services for transitions to decent work over the life course, with particular focus on young and older workers

description.narrative: In 2022-23, the National Employment and Training Centre and the General Federation of Jordanian Trade Unions, in cooperation with the employment service centers at the Ministry of Labour offices, designed and implemented labour market programmes targeted at different vulnerable groups, with a result equaling 4,489 Job Pacements. Furthermore, new employment units have been established in the agriculture sector, and career guidance along with other employment services for young people were considerably enhanced. With the support from the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the ILO supported the employment service centres to ensure the delivery of effective services that varied from registration of job seekers and vacancies, to job matching and career counselling, placement, other active labour market programmes and labour market information and analysis. Capacity building activities including on inclusion of peple with disabilities and gender equality were delivered as well. The ILO supported the government in providing career guidance and employment opportunities for the youth. Several interventions have been implemented in collaboration with the Ministry of Youth, Ministry of Labor, Jordan Cooperative Corporation, and cooperatives at-large.
